steps.text: Cut cucumbers in half lengthwise; scoop out any large seeds. Cut crosswise into very thin slices.
Combine vinegar, sugar, ginger, and salt in a small bowl; mix well. Add cucumber slices; stir to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)
raw_recipe.description: Sunomono is a Japanese cucumber salad made with a light and refreshing rice vinegar, sugar, and ginger dressing for the perfect balance of flavors.
raw_recipe.name: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. Thank you. Some people are so rude! It's called this not that. I added this this and that etc... If people are going to add so much to a recipe, then you are not following the recipe, so how can you rate it one way or another? If you insist on changing so much on a recipe, write your own and don't say you followed somone's recipe (but made your own additions) and then leave them 4 stars after you completely changed the recipe.

First of all, this salad is called "SUNOMONO", not "Sunomo". It's Japanese. I give this recipe 4 stars because it's quite good but I made a few additions that made it 5 stars. I added some thin carrot shavings made with my vegetable peeler. The carrot tastes good with this dressing and adds a really nice touch of colour. I also added several drops of toasted sesame oil and a tiny bit of cracked pepper. Just before serving I added toasted sesame seeds. Everyone loved it :)

Yum! I only added 1/2 the ginger but it was plenty. If you want to have crunchier cucumbers, slice them and salt them heavily. Put them in the fridge overnight then rinse them in a collindar before proceeding with the recipe. It works wonders!

I agree with most of the comments, it's a very simple and tasty recipe. Some comment on just slicing it thin, and leaving the seeds, this will add a little bitterness. So if you don't want to cut it and scoop out the seeds, use an english cucumber, but if using the garden cucumber, remove the seeds. Only other thing is for personal preference is to reduce the sugar from 4-3 teaspoons. Everyones tastes are different so enjoy, say thanks to the creator for taking the time to create the site and posting for everyone to have a better idea on how to make things. And as with every recipe, its a starting point for you to be creative and enjoy it your own way.

I made this recipe (as I have in the past) with three English cucumbers sliced super-thin on a mandoline and added shallot and omitted the ginger. I added the recommended amount of sugar but it was too sweet so I added some Togarashi to increase the heat and I also added some sesame oil (just slight amount) and we really enjoyed it. So tasty. Make sure to drain the liquid coming off the cucumbers before adding any other ingredients (including salt). We drained the liquid three times -- right after the initial slicing, again after adding the salt, and after an hour before we added all the other ingredients. Bonus: if you have other veg around (say, baby carrots or small mushrooms) pour the spare cucumber pickling liquid into a jar/container and then put the carrots or mushrooms or whatever into the jar and let them pickle over a few days. Season the resultant veggies and enjoy :-)

I took the advice of another person here and added carrots and toasted sesame oil. I also put in about a teaspoon of hot honey, and at least a tablespoon of ginger (personal preference). Result: a foot long cuke and affiliated accoutrements were scarfed down in one sitting! I can't stop eating this! Many thanks for this refreshing salad!
I salted the cucumbers and mixed the vinegar and sugar separately (cut the sugar by half) . I omitted fresh ginger because I didn’t have any and sprinkled with a few red pepper flakes.

I've made this for years (at least something almost the same); we love it! I prefer the English type cucumbers because they really don't need peeling and the seeds are very small. I hand slice them as we don't mind if they're not uniformly sliced. I've mostly used cider vinegar but rice vinegar is great also, I've used both. I use similar proportions of sugar and salt and I've sometimes added a few hot pepper flakes, but ginger is a wonderful substitute for this. Often I add some sliced sweet onion to the mix. Delicious!!
I make this but I add a 1/2 bunch of chopped cilantro, and very thinly sliced onion.
I loved the Cucumber Salad. The rice vinegar was not as tart as regular vinegar. I love cucumbers so this salad was great to add to my recipe box. Next time I will add some chopped onions.
Oh this was so good. Tastes just like the Sunomono at our fav restaurant. Fast and easy. Refreshing side to any dinner. I added a dash of toasted sesame oil and some shaved carrot. Yummy.
very easy, very GOOD

Always been a fan of cucumber salad recipes - they're the perfect side dish for summer BBQs, or any time of year. To keep the Asian influence going, I slice my cukes at an angle, so they come out looking like strips of cucumber, not celery (as this illustration shows). Also, I like adding a dash or two of wakame (dried seaweed) and some sesame seeds for extra umami-ness. Finally, I mix a cube of ginger juice (buying a bottle of juice, then freezing in ice cubes is my personal go-to) with the rice vinegar and sugar, and viola! I use English cucumbers because they're seedless, and don't need to be scraped out like traditional cucumbers do.
It was sooo yummy. I will be making it a lot!
This is sooo good!! I did add a few drops of sesame seeds oil! After about 15 minutes marinated I drained off extra dressing and can last beautifully a few days in fridge for snacking
So absolutely refreshing!! I learned that removing the seeds prolongs the life of cucumber slices and keeps them crisp longer. Definitely a keeper, and soooooo simple to make in a hurry.
Good but a lot of water left in the cucs.
Always a winner. I keep a batch of this going at all times during the summer, with our surplus of cucumbers. Even my picky kid eats it. So refreshing and yummy!
I love this salad and I don’t usually eat cucumbers.

I think zucchini would be best due to the water content of cucumbers. It was a crowd favorite at the potluck. I salted the cucumbers and had to pour over at least eight times in total. The flavors were great.
